terms.comment: First “likely, credible” (see probably); then, of people and things, worth approving, acceptable. What is unacceptable is often simply nōn probandum, or id nōn probō, I don’t accept that.
What can be put up with; of an orator, passable (Cic. Brut. 178).

phrases.latin: C. Licinius probābilis ōrātor, jam vērō etiam probātus
phrases.english: Gaius Licinius, an acceptable speaker, and indeed an approved one

phrases.latin: omnia autem brevia tolerābilia esse dēbent, etiamsī magna sunt
phrases.english: but everything short ought to be bearable, even if it is great

sources: Lewis & Short: probabilis · Lewis & Short: tolerabilis
